old: In high-register political, academic, and philosophical Hungarian, the demonstrative cleft construction
new: You know *nem más, mint* and *éppen az, ami* from B2 Unit 65; here they carry Széchenyi's story. In high-register political, academic, and philosophical Hungarian, the demonstrative cleft construction
why: culture unit replays Unit 65: recap

old: The demonstrative 'az' serves as the grammatical subject or predicate head, while the postpositional phrase 'nem más, mint' focuses the true cause.
new: Often the demonstrative 'az' stands before the formula ('A szabadság az nem más, mint ...'), but the formula also works without it; 'nem más, mint' names the true cause.
why: 'postpositional phrase' is wrong: nem más, mint is a fixed formula, not a postposition

old: It was precisely that practical institution-building that was missing from the country, which the count realized by building the Chain Bridge.
new: It was precisely that practical action that was missing from the country, which Széchenyi set in motion with the Chain Bridge.
why: English follows

old: In intellectual debates, scholars contrast false premises
new: You know *nem az a kérdés, hogy …, hanem az, hogy …* from B2 Unit 65, and the pattern of a demonstrative plus a *hogy* clause from B2 Unit 17 (*függetlenül attól, hogy*); *abban rejlik, hogy* follows that pattern. In intellectual debates, scholars contrast false premises
why: culture unit replays Units 65 and 17: recap

old: The greatness of the public education act lay in that it provided mother-tongue education for every nationality.
new: The significance of the public education act lay in that it introduced compulsory schooling.
why: English follows

old: The instrumental pronoun 'azáltal' paired with 'hogy'
new: You know *abból adódóan, hogy* from B2 Unit 65, and the pattern of a demonstrative plus a *hogy* clause from B2 Unit 17 (*függetlenül attól, hogy*); *azáltal, hogy* follows that pattern. The word 'azáltal' (*az* + the postposition *által*) paired with 'hogy'
why: culture unit replays Units 65 and 17: recap; 'instrumental pronoun' is not the right term

old: Political essays often deploy diagnostic cleft predicates
new: You know *nem más, mint* from B2 Unit 65; *éppen abban áll, hogy* follows the pattern of a demonstrative plus a *hogy* clause from B2 Unit 17 (*függetlenül attól, hogy*). Political essays often deploy diagnostic cleft predicates
why: culture unit replays Units 65 and 17: recap

old: Observe Bibó's definitional cleft style: 'Demokratának lenni nem más, mint a félelem hiánya' (To be a democrat is none other than the absence of fear). Such formulations establish foundational ethical benchmarks against which political reality can be critically evaluated at the B2/C1 levels.
new: Definitional clefts state what a concept is: 'Demokratának lenni nem más, mint nem félni' (To be a democrat is none other than not being afraid). This is an illustrative sentence in the style of political essays, not a quotation. Such formulations set out ethical benchmarks against which political reality can be judged.
why: a sentence put in Bibó's mouth that is not his: marked as illustrative; the level label removed

old: The way out originates precisely from acknowledging our mistakes.
new: The way out lies precisely in that we admit our mistakes.
why: English follows

old: The deepest cause of the misery of small Eastern European states is none other than terror due to continuous border instability.
new: According to Bibó, the main cause of the misery of small Eastern European states is none other than terror due to continuous border instability.
why: English follows

old: At the threshold of advanced C1 mastery, the student synthesizes
new: You know all of these patterns from this unit and from B2 Units 17 and 65. This screen puts them together: the student synthesizes
why: C1 label removed; culture unit replays Units 17 and 65: recap
